description: Skelet R3 golden journey: corpus import to cross-client pack recovery integration proof (test-only grain)

compatibility.instructions: Does this grain preserve all contracts: no product code, schema, API, MCP, migration, donor, or config change; one new test file auto-wired into the existing web CI glob? Any changed behavior?

correctness.instructions: Is the journey proof correct: two-version corpus import with changed/added/private artifacts and evolving flow, then search, inspect, similar, compare, flows, steps, changes (4 owner / 3 outsider), pack, cross-transport URI recovery, save idempotency, and outsider no-oracle denial — each step asserting MCP/REST deep-equal parity or transport-correct status? Does the single test prove the full chain without mocks on the agent paths?

evidence.instructions: Is evidence sufficient: new journey test green locally, web/node/worker 123/123, python 209/209, hygiene PASS, graft green, exact-head CI pending? Any passing-test-only claim without integration coverage?

reliability.instructions: Any nondeterminism or resource risk: corpus import is ledger-idempotent with fixed source version, search assertions tolerate multi-hit ordering via parity comparison, pack creation uses fixed titles, no wall-clock or timing assertions, PGlite fixture per run?

scope.instructions: Anything beyond the journey proof: product changes, new tools/routes, embeddings, billing, UI, donor work, or unrelated refactors? Are three-client wire interop and Lens/browser paths correctly left to their existing suites rather than duplicated here?

security.instructions: Do the R2 guarantees hold inside the journey: private vault screen invisible to the outsider via changes (total 3 vs 4, title absent from JSON), unknown flow IDs denied without oracle, error bodies leak-checked on every envelope, no secrets?
